items.text:
प्रणम्य शिरसा विष्णुं त्रैलोक्याधिपतिं प्रभुम् ।
नानाशास्त्रोद्धृतं वक्ष्ये राजनीतिसमुच्चयम् ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
praṇamya śirasā viṣṇuṃ trailokyādhipatiṃ prabhum |
nānāśāstroddhṛtaṃ vakṣye rājanītisamuccayam || 1 ||
items.en: Bowing my head to Lord Vishnu, the master of the three worlds, I will set out a collection of wise rules for rulers, drawn from many sacred books.

items.text:
अधीत्येदं यथाशास्त्रं नरो जानाति सत्तमः ।
धर्मोपदेशं विख्यातं कार्याकार्यं शुभाशुभम् ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
adhītyedaṃ yathāśāstraṃ naro jānāti sattamaḥ |
dharmopadeśaṃ vikhyātaṃ kāryākāryaṃ śubhāśubham || 2 ||
items.en: A good person who studies this in the proper way comes to know what duty teaches, what should and should not be done, and what is good and what is bad.

items.text:
तद् अहं संप्रवक्ष्यामि लोकानां हितकाम्यया ।
येन विज्ञानामात्रेण सर्वज्ञत्वं प्रपद्यते ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
tad ahaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā |
yena vijñānāmātreṇa sarvajñatvaṃ prapadyate || 3 ||
items.en: So, wishing for the good of all people, I will explain it; just by understanding it, one gains a wide knowledge of life.

items.text:
मूर्खशिष्योपदेशेन दुष्टास्त्रीभरणेन च ।
दुःखितैः सम्प्रयोगेण पण्डितो ऽप्य् अवसीदति ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
mūrkhaśiṣyopadeśena duṣṭāstrībharaṇena ca |
duḥkhitaiḥ samprayogeṇa paṇḍito 'py avasīdati || 4 ||
items.en: Even a wise person comes to grief by teaching a foolish pupil, by supporting a wicked woman, and by keeping close company with the miserable.

items.text:
दुष्टा भार्या शठं मित्रं भृत्यश् चोत्तरदायकः ।
ससर्पे च गृहे वासो मृत्युर् एव न संशयः ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
duṣṭā bhāryā śaṭhaṃ mitraṃ bhṛtyaś cottaradāyakaḥ |
sasarpe ca gṛhe vāso mṛtyur eva na saṃśayaḥ || 5 ||
items.en: A wicked wife, a false friend, a servant who talks back, and living in a house with a snake: these are death itself, without doubt.

items.text:
आपदर्थे धनं रक्षेद्दारान् रक्षेध्दनैरपि ।
आत्मानं सततं रक्षेद्दारैरपि धनैरपि ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
āpadarthe dhanaṃ rakṣeddārān rakṣedhdanairapi |
ātmānaṃ satataṃ rakṣeddārairapi dhanairapi || 6 ||
items.en: Save money for hard times; protect your wife even at the cost of money; but always protect yourself, even at the cost of wife and money.

items.text:
आपदार्थे धनं रक्षेच्छ्रीमतश्च किमापदः ।
कदाचिच्चलेता लक्ष्मीःसंचितोऽपिविनश्यति ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
āpadārthe dhanaṃ rakṣecchrīmataśca kimāpadaḥ |
kadāciccaletā lakṣmīḥsaṃcito'pivinaśyati || 7 ||
items.en: Save money for hard times. If you ask what trouble a rich man can have, know that fortune is fickle; even wealth piled up can be lost one day.

items.text:
यस्मिन् देशे न सम्मानो न वृत्तिर्न च बान्धवः ।
न च विद्यागमऽप्यस्ति वासस्तत्र न कारयेत् ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
yasmin deśe na sammāno na vṛttirna ca bāndhavaḥ |
na ca vidyāgama'pyasti vāsastatra na kārayet || 8 ||
items.en: Do not live in a place where you get no respect, no means of living, no relatives, and no chance to learn.

items.text:
धनिकः श्रोत्रियो राजा नदी वैद्यस्तु पञ्चमः ।
पञ्च यत्र न विद्यन्ते न तत्र दिवसं वसेत ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
dhanikaḥ śrotriyo rājā nadī vaidyastu pañcamaḥ |
pañca yatra na vidyante na tatra divasaṃ vaseta || 9 ||
items.en: Do not stay even one day where these five are missing: a rich man, a learned priest, a king, a river, and a doctor.

items.text:
लोकयात्रा भयं लज्जा दाक्षिणायं त्यागशीलता ।
पञ्च यत्र न विद्यन्ते न कुर्य्यात्तत्र सड्गतिम्‍ ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
lokayātrā bhayaṃ lajjā dākṣiṇāyaṃ tyāgaśīlatā |
pañca yatra na vidyante na kuryyāttatra saḍgatim || 10 ||
items.en: Do not make your home among people who lack these five: a way to earn a living, fear of wrong, a sense of shame, kindness, and a giving nature.

items.text:
जानीयात् प्रेषणे भृत्यान् बान्धवान् व्यसनागमे ।
मित्रं चापत्तिकाले तु भार्यां च विभवक्षये ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
jānīyāt preṣaṇe bhṛtyān bāndhavān vyasanāgame |
mitraṃ cāpattikāle tu bhāryāṃ ca vibhavakṣaye || 11 ||
items.en: Test servants when you send them on a task, relatives when trouble comes, a friend in danger, and a wife when wealth is lost.

items.text:
आतुरे व्यसने प्राप्ते दुर्भिक्षे शत्रुसंकटे ।
राजद्वारे श्मशाने च यस्तिष्ठति स बान्धवः ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
āture vyasane prāpte durbhikṣe śatrusaṃkaṭe |
rājadvāre śmaśāne ca yastiṣṭhati sa bāndhavaḥ || 12 ||
items.en: The one who stands by you in sickness, in misfortune, in famine, when enemies attack, at the king's court, and at the cremation ground is your true relative.

items.text:
यो ध्रुवाणि परित्यज्य अध्रुवं परिषेवते ।
ध्रुवाणि तस्य नश्यन्ति अध्रुवं नष्टमेव हि ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
yo dhruvāṇi parityajya adhruvaṃ pariṣevate |
dhruvāṇi tasya naśyanti adhruvaṃ naṣṭameva hi || 13 ||
items.en: One who leaves what is certain and runs after what is uncertain loses what was certain, and the uncertain is lost anyway.

items.text:
वरयेत्कुलजां प्राज्ञो विरूपामपि कन्यकाम् ।
रूपशीलां न नीचस्य विवाहः सद्रॄशे कुले ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
varayetkulajāṃ prājño virūpāmapi kanyakām |
rūpaśīlāṃ na nīcasya vivāhaḥ sadrṝśe kule || 14 ||
items.en: A wise man should marry a girl of a good family even if she is plain, rather than a beautiful one from a low family; marriage is best between equals.

items.text:
नदीनां शस्रपाणीनां नखीनां श्रृड्गिणां तथा ।
विश्वासो नैव कर्तव्यः स्त्रीषुराजकुलेषु च ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
nadīnāṃ śasrapāṇīnāṃ nakhīnāṃ śrṛḍgiṇāṃ tathā |
viśvāso naiva kartavyaḥ strīṣurājakuleṣu ca || 15 ||
items.en: Never put your trust in rivers, in men who carry weapons, in animals with claws or horns, in women, or in royal families.

items.text:
विषाद् अप्य् अमृतं ग्राह्यम् अमेध्याद् अपि काञ्चनम् ।
नीचाद् अप्युत्तमां विद्या स्त्रीरत्नं दुष्कुलाद् अपि ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
viṣād apy amṛtaṃ grāhyam amedhyād api kāñcanam |
nīcād apyuttamāṃ vidyā strīratnaṃ duṣkulād api || 16 ||
items.en: Take nectar even from poison, gold even from filth, the best knowledge even from a lowly person, and a fine wife even from a humble family.

items.text:
स्त्रीणां द्विगुण आहारो लज्जा चापि चतुर्गणा ।
साहसं षड्गुणं चैव कामश् चाष्टगुणः स्मृतः ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
strīṇāṃ dviguṇa āhāro lajjā cāpi caturgaṇā |
sāhasaṃ ṣaḍguṇaṃ caiva kāmaś cāṣṭaguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ || 17 ||
items.en: It is said that women have twice the appetite of men, four times the shyness, six times the daring, and eight times the desire.
